summary: Step B INLINE row engine verified end-to-end in the fullscreen Format editor at 1280x900 on the 'T2' note. INLINE row insertion, caret parking, inter-cell navigation (via INLINE Left/Center/Right), per-cell independent editing, flex-based visual anchoring (display:flex, flex 1 1 0, text-align left/center/right, equal widths ~273px, all cells on same top), Bold formatting inside a cell, and BLOCK path side-effect freedom all PASS. However, TWO critical Step-B scenarios FAIL: (1) Enter inside a cell does NOT exit the row — instead the browser's default splits the cell span, producing a 4-cell row; (2) Backspace at offset 0 of an EMPTY cell does NOT protect the scaffold — the preventDefault never fires. Root cause: the keydown interceptor at FloatingRichTextToolbar.jsx L2051-2088 scopes by `findInlineCell(ed, e.target)`, but for keydown events inside nested contenteditable spans, e.target is the OUTER editor <div> (verified via a probe: {ph:'capture',k:'Enter',tgt:'DIV'}), so findInlineCell returns null and the handler early-exits. The fix is to resolve the caret cell via window.getSelection().getRangeAt(0).startContainer instead of (or as a fallback to) e.target.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): In the keydown handler in /app/frontend/src/notes/editor/FloatingRichTextToolbar.jsx around L2051-2056, resolve the active cell from the SELECTION instead of e.target. Example: `const sel = window.getSelection && window.getSelection(); const node = sel && sel.rangeCount ? sel.getRangeAt(0).startContainer : e.target; const cell = findInlineCell(ed, node);`. The same fix fixes both Enter-exit-row and Backspace-protects-scaffold in one shot, since both branches already use `cell` once they're past the guard. Re-verify ENTER_exits_row and BACKSPACE_protects_scaffold after the fix.

critical_code_review_comments: FloatingRichTextToolbar.jsx is still ~4266 lines. Extracting AlignPanel / HighlightPanel / AppearancePanel AND the INLINE row helpers into their own files is overdue.

The INLINE keydown interceptor uses e.target as the cell probe. e.target in a contenteditable tree is almost always the OUTER editor root — reading the caret from window.getSelection() is the correct source of truth. This same anti-pattern should be audited across the file (grep for `e.target` in keydown handlers).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro for Enter bug: open any note → accordion-fullscreen-* → fullscreen-mode-format → editor innerHTML seeded with a well-formed <div class='ir-irow'> row with 3 <span class='ir-icell' contenteditable='true'> cells → place caret inside center cell via Selection API (selectNodeContents + collapse(false)) → page.keyboard.press('Enter'). Same reproduction (with execCommand('delete') first to empty the right cell) reproduces the Backspace bug. Fix is a one-liner in the keydown handler at FloatingRichTextToolbar.jsx L2055 — switch from e.target to window.getSelection().getRangeAt(0).startContainer.
rca_of_the_issue: The INLINE row keydown interceptor at FloatingRichTextToolbar.jsx L2049-2091 computes the active cell with `findInlineCell(ed, e.target)`. For keydown events in a nested contenteditable=true structure, the event target is the OUTER contenteditable root (the editor <div>), NOT the inner <span data-ir='cell'> that visually holds the caret. findInlineCell therefore walks from the editor <div> up to the editor and returns null — the handler early-exits before it can preventDefault. The browser's default contenteditable Enter semantics then split the cell span, and the default Backspace eats the scaffold boundary. The caret cell must be derived from window.getSelection() instead.
